the luster of bracelets flashes.*
notes: The 1912/13 ed. (checked against the scan) reads "বাজত থর, নাহি অতুল, ঝলকে কমুক কাঁতি" (bājata thara, nāhi atula); "bracelets" follows G "কঙ্গক" (kaṅkaṇa?); কমুক (kamuka) in A is possibly kanaka, "golden luster." The sense of the line is not quite clear.

verses_en.text:
Through the paths of the sky roam
countless throngs, eagerness in their hearts;
they deem their sight fulfilled,
beholding the wedding of Gaura the groom.

Extolling the charming customs
of Mishra's house, their whole bodies thrilling,
they form ever new desires —
they cannot hold their composure.

The form of the matchless Lord and [His] beloved
they take in, filling their eyes.
How much will Narahari tell? All
offer their lives for Them.

Again (in any raga):
Ah, I die, I die! The celestial women,
seeing the wedding of the moon of Nadia,
swimming in that ocean of beauty, all
satisfy their thirsty eyes.

One says to another: "Look, the heart of Mishra
Sanatana cannot contain his happiness!
With what longing he has given his daughter to Krishna,*
and how much he says, offering various gifts!"
notes: "To Krishna" — কৃষ্ণে (kṛṣṇe): so in the 1912/13 ed. (checked against the scan: "কৃষ্ণে কন্যা দান, করি কত সাধে"); in the OCR of the 1960 ed. the word is garbled. Narahari calls Gaura Krishna.

verses_en.text:
Someone says: "Having seated his daughter at the left
of his son-in-law, he deems himself blessed.
He performs the homa rite, but his mind is not on it:
he keeps gazing at the moon-like face."

Someone says: "Look, Mishra's wife
is as if mad in the wedding bustle.
On so many pretexts she gazes at Narahari's Lord;*
in her delight her feet do not touch the ground."
notes: "Narahari's Lord" (narahari-nātha): the Lord of the poet Narahari, i.e. Gaura; the poet's usual signature in a pada (likewise in 1570, 1574).

verses_en.text:
Again (in any raga):
Gods and goddesses in delight
all speak of the wedding in soft voices.

Fortunate are the people of Nadia:
the wedding has taken place — seeing it, all rejoiced.

The brahmanas in whose homes there are beautiful daughters
all lament greatly in their minds:

"To give our daughter to such a groom
we were not able — such happiness is not in our fate."

Thus someone says so much;
everyone praises Sanatana Mishra.

The fortunate Sanatana Mishra
completed the homa and all [the other rites].

Gazing at his daughter and son-in-law,
[he feels:] moment by moment happiness grows, and his heart overflows.

Who can describe the customs?
Again and again the women raise the cry, "Jaya!"

To take Devi Vishnupriya and Gorachand
into the bridal chamber — who can stay calm?*
notes: "Bridal chamber": bāsara-ghara, the room in the bride's house where the newlyweds spend the first night surrounded by the women of the family, who joke with the groom.

verses_en.text:
Narahari's Lord, Gora Raya,
goes into the bridal chamber with great delight in His heart.

Again (in any raga):
Gora, the delight of Nadia,
enters the bridal chamber —
the thief of the life of ever new young women. (Refrain.)

The wives of noble families, with joy in their hearts,
taking Vishvambhara and Vishnupriya,
in a most sweet manner seat [Them] in the bridal chamber
and with unblinking eyes gaze at those faces.

One, longing to touch, smiling, smiling,
smears fragrant sandal paste on [His] body;
another, preparing a box of betel cups,
playfully sets [it] before [Him].

Someone, under the pretext of jest, does so much:
swaying, she leans against [His] body, her heart thrilling;
someone stands before Narahari's Lord
and gracefully offers a handful of flowers.

Again (in any raga):
In the bridal chamber Gora Raya
intoxicates millions of Madanas with His beauty.

The wives of noble families, with happiness in their hearts,
give over their eyes to the moon-like face.

One, drawing veil over veil,
says something with a slight smile.

Her whole body fills with thrills,
and she covers it with her cloth.

One, standing beside another,
trembles, overcome by rasa.*
notes: The 1912/13 ed. (checked against the scan) reads "কাঁপে সেনা রসের আবেশে"; সেনা is understood as সে না ("she"; cf. 1291, 1478); "মেনা" in the OCR is a recognition error.

verses_en.text:
Someone, her heart extremely restless,
offers her life for [His] reddish feet.*
notes: "Reddish feet" — "রাঙ্গাপায়" (rāṅgā pāya): so in the 1912/13 ed. (checked against the scan: "নিছয়ে জীবন রাঙ্গাপায়"); the 1960 ed. (OCR) has "রাধা পায়," probably a recognition error.

verses_en.text:
How much merriment there is in the bridal chamber —
who will be able to tell how much?

In Narahari's mind there is this hope:
will I see all these pastimes?

Again (in any raga):
In the bridal chamber Gora Raya
happily passes the night with Vishnupriya.

There is no end to telling of the merriment;
Sanatana with all his kin is lost in bliss.

At daybreak Gaurahari
became joyful, having performed the kushandika and other rites.*
notes: Kushandika: the rite before the sacred fire that concludes the wedding (performed after the wedding night).

verses_en.text:
"I will go to My home,"
He submits to the respected Sanatana Mishra.

Sanatana with effort keeps his composure
to send off his jewel of a son-in-law.

Consoling his daughter in so many ways,
he gave her over, entrusting her, holding Vishvambhara's hand.

At the time of departure Gaurahari
bows with great joy to the respected people.

How all of them longed to do this!*
Placing paddy and durva grass on His head, they bless [Him].
notes: Following A/B karite; the 1960 ed. reads kahite: "Who can describe the longing of them all?"

verses_en.text:
Mishra's wife, sending off her daughter and son-in-law,
cannot keep her composure.

As Gora sets out for home,
the brahmanas on all sides chant the Vedas.

The women raise the cry, "Jaya!";
various instruments sound, the bards recite eulogies.

Beholding Narahari's Lord,
all perform the auspicious rites befitting departure.

Again (in any raga):
The ornament of Vraja, Gaura, the finest of moons, having performed the wedding, intent on delightful play,
goes with His beloved to His home — a supreme, wondrous beauty.
He rides in a palanquin, flashing; the nectar-stream of His beauty overflows;
His matchless adornment, which draws the eyes, enchants the minds of all people.

Ceaselessly the cry "Jaya, jaya!" resounds; countless women and men behold
and say to one another: "It is as if Lakshmi and the Lord of Lakshmi — both of Them are sporting."
The panegyrists, their minds exceedingly delighted, extol ever new deeds full of rasa;
a great tumult rises, again and again the Vedas sound, bodies thrill.*
notes: "A great tumult" is understood as ḍambara ("noise, pomp; multitude"); the 1912/13 ed. (checked against the scan) reads "ভূরি ভূম্বুর(?) করত ঘন," the 1960 ed. (OCR) "ভূগ্গর"; the spelling remains unclear even on the scan. The same word occurs in 1612 ("a vast throng").

verses_en.text:
Instruments of many kinds — muraja, mardala, trisari, kundali, pataha, pushkala;
"kuku nunu nunu nu dha" — hosts of musicians sweetly play on various [instruments].*
Dancing girls and rows of dancers dance, calling out "ta dhik dhikita dhini
nini dhenna dhiki taka"; they keep the tala, and in the movements of their feet the radiance of their bodies flashes.
notes: The 1912/13 ed. (checked against the scan) reads "মরুজ মর্দ্দল, ত্রিসরি কুণ্ডলি পটহ পুষ্কল, কুকু নুনু নুনু, নু ধা" — trisari, kundali, pataha, pushkala (a drum); the drum syllables follow the scan of A; in G they are garbled ("বুকু হুম, সু সুধা").

verses_en.text:
Jati, shruti, svara-grama, murchhana, tana, ever new, new, new alapas —
hearing them, the deer leave the forest, and throngs of connoisseurs hasten near.
All around the house there is a vast uproar; Narahari Dasa's heart overflows.
At the hour of godhuli, having rested on the charming bank of the Suradhuni, He comes home.*
notes: Godhuli: dusk, the "hour of cow-dust," when the herds return home. The Suradhuni ("river of the gods") is the Ganga.

verses_en.text:
Again (in any raga):
Gorachand, having married,
comes home exceedingly jubilant.

Unseen, the gods
shower flowers along the whole way.

In Nadia there is an ocean of happiness;
someone tells Mother Shachi about the wedding.

Hearing the great clamor of instruments,
Devi Shachi was overwhelmed with bliss.

Shachi Ai, outside the house,
with the chaste women stands watching the road.

Gora, with everyone, slowly, slowly
approaching, stepped down from the palanquin at the door.

Ai, seeing her son and daughter-in-law,
waves things around [them] and casts them away — countless things.

Lovingly kissing the moon-like face,
she enters the house, leading her daughter-in-law and son.

Vishvambhara with Vishnupriya
sits on the throne; all the associates behold [it].

The women give the cry "ulu-lu-lu";
the whole world became filled with auspiciousness.

The bards recite eulogies;
the brahmanas ceaselessly chant the Vedas.

All joyfully play various instruments;
how much can Narahari tell with one mouth?

Again (in any raga):
Gora, the jewel of virtues, the crown of the accomplished,
His heart supremely delighted —
the many people, stirred by the wedding,
[He] gives them leave.

Bards, actors, singers, musicians,
beggars — a vast throng —
He gives them all many clothes, ornaments and wealth,
fulfilling their desires.

Most skilled in the sweetest words,
He satisfies everyone.
All went together to their own homes,
singing the glory of Gaurahari.*
notes: So in the 1960 ed.; in the 1912/13 ed. (checked against the scan) the strophe is shorter: "অতি হি সুমধুর, বচনে সুনিপুণ, গৌরহরি যশ গায়" — the words "পরিতোষ করই সভায়। চলল নিজ-নিজ গেহে সবে মিলি" ("He satisfies everyone. All went together to their own homes") are absent from it.

verses_en.text:
Sri Shachi showed all the women,
each one, great honor;
says Narahari: all of them happily
went to their homes.

O Srinivasa, the joy that there was at Vishvambhara's wedding
awakens in the heart.

Here Gaurahari sat with Vishnupriya,
and His mother watched it, filling her eyes.

How much affection Ai shows to Vishnupriya —
it is impossible to tell all of it with one mouth.

How much shall I tell of Devi Vishnupriya's conduct?
She devoted herself to the service of Vishnu and the service of Sri Shachi.

What shall I say? By the service of Devi Vishnupriya
Ai passes day and night in great bliss.

Vishvambhara enjoys [His pastimes] in supreme bliss;
as He enters youth, the beauty of [His] body is enchanting.

Always [He is] beautifully adorned with divine garlands and sandal paste;
[His] body is decorated with fine garments and ornaments.
Gora, the son of Shachi, the enchanter of the world,

bhakti-ratnakara.title: Дома Санатаны Мишры и Кашинатхи: свадьба с Вишнуприей
bhakti-ratnakara.summary: Ишана показывает дом Санатаны Мишры, раджа-пандита, отдавшего дочь Вишнуприю Вишвамбхаре, и жилище Кашинатхи Пандита, много потрудившегося ради этой свадьбы.

verses.text:
Вот, смотри, — дом Санатаны Мишры,
который был Раджа-пандитом, во всём выдающимся.

Дочь Санатаны Мишры — Вишнуприя;
одними устами не могу рассказать о её деяниях.

Санатана Мишра с великой радостью в сердце
здесь отдал дочь Вишвамбхаре.
Смотри — жилище Кашинатхи Пандита;

verses_en.text:
Look, here is the house of Sanatana Mishra,
who was the Raja-pandita, eminent in every respect.

Sanatana Mishra's daughter is Vishnupriya;
with one mouth I cannot tell of her deeds.

Sanatana Mishra, with great joy in his heart,
gave his daughter to Vishvambhara here.
Look at the dwelling of Kashinatha Pandita;

sanyal.title: Тилака учеников; женитьба на Шри Вишнуприе-деви
sanyal.summary: Нанесение знака тилаки на лоб обязательно для Его учеников. Различие между трипундрой и урдхва-пундрой. Является ли знак тилаки «символом»? Нимай Пандит избегает общества женщин. Этим пренебрегает лжесекта гаура-нагари. Писания осуждают половое влечение. Духовная любовь и плотское вожделение. Обвинение в том, что Шри Чайтанья был не в здравом уме. Вторая женитьба Господа. Таинство брака. Поведение Шри Чайтаньи тождественно лиле Шри Кришны и вместе с тем отлично от неё. Шри Чайтанья принимает на Себя роль Шри Радхики. Сватом выступает Кашинатха Пандит. Обряд *адхиваса*.

sanyal.title: Свадебные обряды; Буддхиманта Хан; значение женитьбы Господа; Шри, Бху и Нила
sanyal.summary: Свадебные обряды. Буддхиманта Хан. Значение женитьбы Господа. Личность Шри Вишнуприи-деви. Шри, Бху и Нила. Взаимозависимый характер функций различных энергий Господа. Значение последовавшего затем отречения Господа от мира.

advaita-prakasha.title: Женитьба на Вишнуприи, дочери Санатаны Мишры
advaita-prakasha.summary: Преданные и друзья устраивают женитьбу Гауранги на Вишнуприи, дочери раджа-пандита Санатаны Мишры, которого Адвайта называет Сатраджитом, а её — Шри Сатьей; в доме Шачи великий праздник; рассказ передан Ишане Ачьютой.

verses.text: Затем преданные Гауры и любимые друзья устроили там женитьбу Гауранги.
Раджа-пандит Санатана Мишра, царь брахманов, — Господь называет его явлением Шри Сатраджита.
Его дочь Вишнуприя — венец целомудренных, полная всех добродетелей, кладезь нектара красоты.
Господь называет её Шри Сатьей, энергией наслаждения, Лакшми. Шри Гаурачандра взял её в жёны.
По этому случаю в доме Шачи был великий праздник; обретя невестку, Шачи пребывала в радости.
Это благое сказание поведал мне Шри Ачьюта; я изложил лишь малую долю его сути.
Уповая на стопы Шри Чайтаньи и Шри Адвайты, Ишана Нагара повествует «Адвайта-пракашу».

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
Now hear a wondrous account: the all-knowing Ishvara Puri came to Navadvipa.
The Lord calls him the embodiment of the radiant rasa (ujjvala-rasa): in whoever sees him loving devotion awakens.
A supreme Vaishnava, detached and dispassionate, Puri first stayed at Advaita's house.
Seeing the radiant great sannyasi, Sitanatha said, "Obeisance to Narayana," and prostrated Himself before him.
Seeing Sri Advaita, Puri understood to himself: "Surely this is the original acharya, by whose will Krishna appears."
Learning that he was Sri Ishvara Puri, the disciple of Sri Madhavendra, the Lord shed tears of love.
Then the waves of their talk about Krishna rose, and little by little both sank into the ocean of the nectar of love.
Now they wept, now laughed, now lost consciousness, now roared deeply like lions.
After some time the external awareness of both returned, and Sitanatha fed the king among Puris.
Then Puri wandered about Navadvipa and at an auspicious moment beheld Sri Gauranga.
The radiance of Gaurachandra's body is like millions of suns; seeing it, Puri felt a surge of mahabhava.
Puri thought: "He is truly Bhagavan Himself, abiding in Navadvipa in the form of Gaura."
Vishvambhara, seeing the radiant king among Puris, thought: "This is a great bhagavata, the best of sannyasis."
Gaura hastened over and bowed to him. Puri said: "The desire of your heart will be fulfilled."
In conversation they came to know each other and, discussing the shastras, floated in bliss.
Then Gaura insistently invited the king among Puris and fed him with various dishes.
Puri rested there for some days and then, seeing that the time for Gaura's manifestation had not yet come, went off to the holy places.
One day Sri Gauranga said to Shachi: "Mother, I shall go with My disciples to the eastern land.
I shall soon return from My journey. Do not be sad or anxious about Me.
Stay at home, Mother, and worship Krishna: abiding in the bliss of love, you will know no torment."
Having said this, He bowed at Shachi's feet, and His mother blessed Him with pain in her heart.
And so Gaurachandra set out for the east and appeared at the house of Padmanabha.
Mahaprabhu's companion, Lokanatha Chakravarti, called his father and said: "Come out to meet Him!"
Padmanabha Chakravarti is most pure, a vessel of the mercy of Sri Advaitachandra.
Krishna in the form of Gaura had revealed Himself in Navadvipa — by the power of the Lord's mercy he dimly knew of it.
Even before, in ecstasy, he had understood: "Krishna Himself in the form of Gaura has come to my house."
The brahmana came out to meet Him with a cloth tied round his neck; seeing Gauranga, he recognized Him at once.
He prostrated himself before Mahaprabhu, while Gaura, saying "Vishnu, Vishnu," turned aside.
Padmanabha said: "Gaura, do not deceive me: the hidden truth about You abides in the hearts of the devotees.
You are Krishna Himself, full of all rasas: You have descended Yourself to deliver the souls."
Having said this, he offered Him a divine seat, and Gaura, remembering Vishnu, sat down.
Padmanabha honoured Him according to all the rules, and Mahaprabhu stayed there several days.
A great rumour went round: "Nimai Pandita has come!" — and the pandits and all the learned came.
Hundreds came to see Him, counting themselves fortunate: children, old men, youths and all the women.
A great uproar arose — all wanted to see Gaura. After some thought, Gora went up to the upper storey of the house.
Gaura's form is the radiance of the brightest gold, His arms reach to His knees, He is a well of the nectar of rasa.
Restless eyes, a face like a blossoming lotus; with His left arm He embraced Achyuta round the neck.
All bathed in the Ganga nectar of His wondrous beauty; some by good fortune became intoxicated by it.
Some in the ecstasy of love shed many tears, others, raising their arms, danced joyfully.
At night the learned gathered for a great assembly; on all sides lamps were burning like jewels.
Gaura came to the assembly with His disciples, and all, seeing Him, rose respectfully.
In the midst of the assembly Gaurachandra sat like the moon, and the learned surrounded Him like stars.
There was a learned brahmana there, a Tarka-chudamani, skilled in the shastras, the crown of pandits.
He raised a question of logic, and as soon as Sri Gauranga heard it, He refuted it.
That brahmana defended his position again and again, and Mahaprabhu refuted it with ease.
The opponent's position collapsed and could not be established, and then the pandits admitted themselves defeated.
All said: "We had heard that Nimai is called Vidyasagara — His divine learning has been proved."
One day a best of brahmanas, a devotee of Vishnu, joined his palms and said to Mahaprabhu:
"Seeing the world enveloped in the terrible sins of Kali, tell us: how will the souls be delivered?"
Hearing this, Mahaprabhu said: "The essence of all is the name of Hari: by hearing and accepting it the souls will be delivered.
Apart from the name of Hari, the souls have no other way: through the Name all sins are destroyed and pure devotion is attained."
Hearing this, the best of brahmanas was filled with the jubilation of love and, crying "Hari!", danced and wept, forgetting the external world.
Seeing this, all the unbelievers laughed, while the minds of Krishna and the Vaishnavas were well pleased.
Great was the good fortune of Padmanabha Chakravarti, to whose house Sri Chaitanya came.
Then Gaura came to the bank of the Padmavati; seeing the Padma, Gora said with joy in His heart:
"This Padmavati is a second body of Lakshmi: bathing in her surely destroys sins."
And so on the bank of that holy river Padmavati Gora settled in a beautiful spot and joyfully passed His time.
The fragrance of Gauranga spread in all directions, and the sadhus began to say to one another:
"On the eastern bank of the Ganga is an abode of the wise — Navadvipa; from there a mighty pandit has come —
Nimai Pandita, with the title Vidyasagara, who composed a commentary called the Vidyasagara."
Hearing of this, many learned men came there and were purified by seeing Gauranga and conversing with Him.
Teachers came with various gifts and joyfully conversed with Gaura.
Many students learned in the shastras came to study: after studying with Him a little, they received scholarly titles.
Meanwhile in Navadvipa Lakshmi-devi, bitten by the serpent of separation from Sri Gauranga, disappeared from this world.
After some days Sriman Shachinandana decided to return to His own home.
At that time a certain eminent righteous man, having seen a dream, came to Mahaprabhu.
Seeing Gaura, he prostrated himself with the eight limbs of his body at His lotus feet and secretly revealed the whole substance of his dream.
Gaura said: "Keep this secret. And now set out for Kashi.
In due time you will meet Me there, and the desire of your heart will surely be fulfilled."
His name was Tapana Mishra, simple at heart; at Mahaprabhu's command he set out for Kashi.
Having thus made East Bengal fortunate, Vishvambhara set out for home with great wealth.
Then Sri Gauranga arrived in Navadvipa; hearing of Lakshmi's disappearance, He expressed sorrow.
Seeing Mother Sri Shachi in great sorrow, He consoled her with various arguments.
Then Gaura's devotees and dear friends arranged there the marriage of Gauranga.
The court pandit Sanatana Mishra, king of brahmanas — the Lord calls him the appearance of Sri Satrajit.
His daughter Vishnupriya is the crown of chaste women, full of all virtues, a mine of the nectar of beauty.
The Lord calls her Sri Satya, the pleasure potency, Lakshmi. Sri Gaurachandra took her as His wife.
On this occasion there was a great festival in Shachi's house; having obtained a daughter-in-law, Shachi lived in joy.
This auspicious account was told me by Sri Achyuta; I have set forth only a small part of its substance.
Placing his hope in the feet of Sri Chaitanya and Sri Advaita, Ishana Nagara tells the Advaita-prakasha.
